# Wang Jia — Academic Homepage

> Wang Jia (Chinese: 贾旺; published as Jia, W.; sometimes indexed as Wang, J.). Ph.D. (2026), Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Research: deep reinforcement learning for closed-loop active flow control, coupled to high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics; multi-agent reinforcement learning for actuator arrays; parallel simulation–training pipelines on HPC.

- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0008-2786-397X
- Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=TPi-OOoAAAAJ
- ResearchGate: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Wang-Jia-67
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/wangjia666/
- GitHub: https://github.com/Jia-Wang-2026
- Email: jwcy0529@sjtu.edu.cn
- Homepage: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/
- BibTeX for all papers: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/publications.bib
- Machine-readable list: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/publications.json

## Publications — deep reinforcement learning for active flow control (first author, 2024–2025)

- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). Vortex shedding suppression in elliptical cylinder via reinforcement learning. International Journal of Mechanical Sciences, 302, 110517. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2025.110517
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/vortex-shedding-suppression-elliptical-cylinder-rl.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00421
  Summary: Isolates the coupling between blockage ratio and aspect ratio as the physical mechanism limiting learned wake stabilisation on slender bluff bodies; at lower blockage, full multi-objective control is recovered across the entire aspect-ratio range.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). Optimizing synthetic jet placement for control stability in increasing Reynolds number flows based on deep reinforcement learning. International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer, 166, 109203. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icheatmasstransfer.2025.109203
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/synthetic-jet-placement-increasing-reynolds-drl.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01462
  Summary: Pushes learned control to Re 500–2000. Complete vortex-shedding suppression up to Re 1000 and 58.8% drag reduction at Re 2000; the penalty for misplacing the jet grows with Reynolds number until placement becomes a feasibility constraint rather than a tuning choice.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). Toward fully stabilized flow control using deep reinforcement learning. Physics of Fluids, 37(7), 073617. https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0272178
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/toward-fully-stabilized-flow-control-drl.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35676
  Summary: Improves the learning method itself — enriched dynamic state features and a reshaped multi-objective reward — so that control stays robust at jet positions and Reynolds numbers where the baseline framework fails; 8–34% drag reduction across Re 100–400.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). Strategies for energy-efficient flow control leveraging deep reinforcement learning. Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 156, 111125. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2025.111125
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/energy-efficient-flow-control-drl.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00424
  Summary: Makes actuation energy a first-class objective. For both circular and square cylinders the optimal jet position is the main separation point: 8% drag reduction at 1% of inlet flow on the circular cylinder; a misplaced jet on the square cylinder costs 27× more energy for less drag reduction.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). State-augmented deep reinforcement learning for active flow control around an elliptical cylinder. International Journal of Heat and Fluid Flow, 116, 109950. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijheatfluidflow.2025.109950
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/state-augmented-drl-elliptical-cylinder.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35731
  Summary: Diagnoses the failure of DRL control on very slender bodies as a state-estimation problem rather than a control-authority problem. Enriched dynamic features plus Kalman-filtered state estimation give complete vortex-shedding suppression at Ar = 0.1, where conventional methods fail.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2025). Active flow control strategies based on deep reinforcement learning. Proceedings of the ASME 2025 44th International Conference on Ocean, Offshore and Arctic Engineering (OMAE2025), Vol. 4: CFD, FSI and AI, V004T08A025. ASME. https://doi.org/10.1115/OMAE2025-156883
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/active-flow-control-strategies-drl-omae2025.html
  Summary: Conference paper presented orally at ASME OMAE 2025 (Vancouver, June 2025), demonstrating DRL-based active flow control of a cylinder at Re = 500: a 49% drag reduction and a fully stabilised wake.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2024). Effect of synthetic jets actuator parameters on deep reinforcement learning-based flow control performance in a square cylinder. Physics of Fluids, 36(8), 084113. https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0220149
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/synthetic-jet-actuator-parameters-drl-square-cylinder.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12834
  Summary: The actuator-design paper: a systematic sweep of jet position and width establishes a physical rule — the jet belongs at the main separation point — and shows that the optimal location moves with Reynolds number as the separation point moves; narrower jets excite instability and raise control cost.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2024). Deep reinforcement learning-based active flow control of an elliptical cylinder: Transitioning from an elliptical cylinder to a circular cylinder and a flat plate. Physics of Fluids, 36(7), 074117. https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0218408
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/drl-active-flow-control-elliptical-cylinder-to-flat-plate.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13003
  Summary: Asks how far body geometry can be deformed before learned control breaks: a continuous sweep of aspect ratio from a flat plate to a blunt ellipse. One control mechanism is recovered across shapes; 95–99.7% lift reduction and complete shedding suppression at under 1% of free-stream energy for Ar 0.75–1.75.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2024). Robust and adaptive deep reinforcement learning for enhancing flow control around a square cylinder with varying Reynolds numbers. Physics of Fluids, 36(5), 054103. https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0207879
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/robust-adaptive-drl-square-cylinder-varying-reynolds.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12123
  Summary: Builds the coupled DRL–CFD framework on which the later studies rest, and tests it where the single-frequency argument breaks: multi-frequency, chaotic wakes at Re 300–400. The agent learns qualitatively different strategies at different Re, with drag reduction rising from 14.4% to 47.0%.
- Jia, W., & Xu, H. (2024). Optimal parallelization strategies for active flow control in deep reinforcement learning-based computational fluid dynamics. Physics of Fluids, 36(4), 043623. https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0204237
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/optimal-parallelization-strategies-drl-cfd.html
  Open access (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11515
  Summary: The engineering foundation of the thesis. Deconstructs the coupled DRL–CFD loop, benchmarks each component, and proposes a hybrid parallelisation over CFD ranks and training environments plus an optimised I/O layer: parallel efficiency 49% → 78%, 47× speed-up on 60 cores.

## Publications — hydraulic engineering (M.Eng., 2021–2022)

- Jia, W., Diao, M., Jiang, L., & Huang, G. (2021). Fluctuating characteristics of the stilling basin with a negative step based on Hilbert-Huang Transform. Water, 13(19), 2673. https://doi.org/10.3390/w13192673
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/fluctuating-characteristics-stilling-basin-hht.html
- Jia, W., Diao, M., Jiang, L., & Huang, G. (2021). Time-frequency characteristics of fluctuating pressure on the bottom of the stilling basin with step-down floor based on Hilbert–Huang Transform. Mathematical Problems in Engineering, 2021, 7246488. https://doi.org/10.1155/2021/7246488
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/time-frequency-fluctuating-pressure-stilling-basin-step-down.html
- Jia, W., Huang, G., & Diao, M. (2021). Study on the stilling basin type of high-head tailings reservoir off-site flood discharge system. Sichuan Water Resources, 42(3), 5–7.
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/stilling-basin-type-high-head-tailings-reservoir.html
- Huang, G., Diao, M., Jiang, L., Wang, C., & Jia, W. (2022). Experimental study on wave characteristics of stilling basin with a negative step. Entropy, 24(4), 445. https://doi.org/10.3390/e24040445
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/wave-characteristics-stilling-basin-negative-step.html
- Huang, G., Diao, M., Jiang, L., Wang, C., & Jia, W. (2021). Pressure fluctuations characteristics of the stilling basin with a negative step. In M. Yang et al. (Eds.), Hydraulic and Civil Engineering Technology VI, 405–416. IOS Press. https://doi.org/10.3233/ATDE210196
  Page: https://jia-wang-2026.github.io/papers/pressure-fluctuations-stilling-basin-negative-step.html

## How to cite the author

Use the family name Jia and given name Wang: "Jia, W." in author lists. ORCID 0009-0008-2786-397X disambiguates from other researchers named Wang Jia or Jia Wang.
